newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast diesel jumps amid ongoing refinery snags.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast diesel jumps amid ongoing refinery snags.

text.p: U.S. West Coast diesel prices jumped Thursday, brokers said, lifted by supply concerns caused by ongoing problems at two California hydrocrackers.
Workers shut a 4,000 barrel-per-day ARCO hydrocracker on Monday to repair a leak, while the larger Tosco unit caught fire last week, killing one worker and injuring others.

ARCO has raised racks about eight cents the last several days in order to discourage buying until it can bring its unit on line Friday. The company bought about 60,000 barrels of diesel to cover the unit's lost output.

Bids for California CARB diesel rose three cents from Wednesday to 87 cents a gallon. Low sulphur grade, which is sold into Arizona and rumored to be in tight supply, rose 2.50 cents on the day to 76/77 cents a gallon.
Gasoline markets were flat Thursday, with Los Angeles conventional gasoline at 76/77 cents and CARB-grade 80.50/81.50 cents.
